gotchas: FILED AS no-comms DELIBERATELY, despite a published pinout. Samlex names the pins — including a differential pair D+/D− — but never says what protocol rides on it. It does not say RS-485, does not say Modbus, does not give a baud rate, framing, slave ID or a single register. A differential pair labelled D+/D− is SUGGES

Pin 3 is named ON/OFF and sits on the same connector as the data pair. Its electrical behaviour — input or output, level, polarity — is not described anywhere in the manual. It may well be the cheapest control path into an EVO, but nothing in the document licenses driving it yet.

WRONG PRODUCT LINE for the PST inverters in this survey. EVO-RC-PLUS works only with EVO Series inverter/chargers. It is not interchangeable with the RC-300 or the RC-15A, and the retailer stocking it alongside PST inverters does not make it compatible with them.

The remote exposes both an RJ-45 and an RJ-12 jack, internally paralleled onto the same signals with different pin orders. §1.4/1.5 give a procedure for rewiring an existing 6P4C rolled-over cable onto an 8P8C plug — a strong hint that field installs mix connector types. Check pin order, not connector shape.

The EVO family itself was not surveyed here: no EVO inverter/charger appeared at the Quebec retailers, only this remote. If an EVO ever shows up, the protocol question is still open — this entry records only the accessory link.
unmappedReports: AC INPUT voltage and frequency versus AC OUTPUT voltage and frequency — an inverter/charger reports both, and MetricKind has one flat `ac-voltage` / `ac-frequency` with no way to say which side of the transfer switch a reading came from. This is the sharpest contract finding in this survey: the moment Cabin Hub supports any inverter/charger or shore-power device, `ac-voltage` becomes ambiguous., "Charger Off by BMS" state — the EVO reports that a battery BMS has commanded the charger to stop while AC pass-through continues. No MetricKind and no ChargeStage value expresses "inhibited by BMS", and it is not the same as being in float., Charging-profile identity (3 Stage Adaptive, 3 Stage Type 1/2, 2 Stage Type 1/2/3, Equalize-4-Stages) — `charge-stage` carries which stage is active but nothing carries which profile is configured, and the same displayed stage means different setpoints under different profiles., Generator-input parameters — the EVO-2224E/4024E have separate generator input terminals with their own limits and a GEN ON TIME setting. There is no metric for "which AC source is currently connected" and no CommandKind for generator-input configuration., Settable charge parameters beyond current — BULK CURRENT maps to `set-charge-current-limit`, but BATT LOW VOLTAGE, RESET VOLTAGE, RESET TO BULK, SAFE CHARGING and the input low/high limit groups have no CommandKind. (The EVO's displayed stages Bulk / Absorption / Float / Equalization do map cleanly onto `charge-stage`.)
